title: Password & Security Analyzer
short_description: Learn how security systems analyze passwords and authentication strings for repeated characters, prefix patterns, suspicious sequences, binary security properties, and unique character substrings.

real_world_context.problem: A security system needs to inspect passwords and authentication strings for repeated characters, registered security prefixes, suspicious patterns, enabled binary security properties, and continuous sections containing unique characters.
real_world_context.why_it_matters: Efficient string-processing and bit-manipulation algorithms help security systems analyze authentication data quickly and identify structural patterns as the amount of security-related data increases.

learning_objectives: Understand how passwords and authentication strings can be represented using strings.
Apply Sliding Window techniques to analyze fixed-size sections of passwords.
Understand how a Trie supports efficient prefix-based security rule searching.
Apply KMP Pattern Matching to locate suspicious patterns efficiently.
Use bit manipulation to count set bits in binary security codes.
Find the longest substring containing no repeated characters.
Understand how different string algorithms can be applied to password and authentication analysis.
Understand why algorithm efficiency matters when processing large amounts of security data.

real_world_mapping.password: String representing a user's authentication password
real_world_mapping.authentication_string: String generated or submitted during authentication
real_world_mapping.security_prefix: Registered sequence of characters used by a security rule
real_world_mapping.prefix_search: Searching for a registered security prefix within a password
real_world_mapping.suspicious_pattern: Known sequence of characters searched for in an authentication log
real_world_mapping.security_code: Integer representing encoded binary security properties
real_world_mapping.set_bit: Enabled security property represented by a binary 1
real_world_mapping.unique_substring: Continuous section of a password containing no repeated characters
real_world_mapping.character_window: Fixed-size section of a password inspected for repeated characters
real_world_mapping.security_analysis: Process of examining authentication data for structural patterns and properties

completion_message: You have completed the Password & Security Analyzer mission. You have learned how sliding windows, Trie operations, KMP pattern matching, bit manipulation, and unique-substring techniques can be applied to password analysis, authentication monitoring, security-rule searching, and security data processing.
